summary: NATURE art/production review of the 9 standard per-run figures (exemplar run 15, Output/run_15/, rendered by macros/*.C with radStyle.h; same macro serves all 14 run pages, so every defect is x14). Overall: the house style (inside-panel text titles, teal/orange/red palette, labeled axes with units, per-panel annotations) is applied to about two-thirds of the set and those figures are close to publication grade. The set is let down by two figures that break the style entirely and by recurring mechanical defects that a single radStyle/macro pass would fix. CROSS-CUTTING (ranked): [critical] Clipped/garbled canvas-top titles on QCv2_MIP.png and QCv2_align.png — ROOT TPaveText titles are drawn above the frame and cut at the canvas edge, leaving illegible glyph fragments; move titles inside the frame as done in TransferFit/MCPThreshold (this is the one fix that must happen before any external showing). [critical] QCv2_align right panel: five unlabeled ROOT-default-color curves (red/green/blue/black/gray), no legend, red+green pairing is colorblind-unsafe — unusable as published. [major] Missing y-axis titles: all 4 panels of QCv2_MIP, left panel of QCv2_align, all 4 panels of Integrity_health (which also lack an x-axis title "channel index"). [major] Thin amber/orange strokes on white (XCETCheck right panel, TransferFit annotations on beige, BestTiming cap-6 line) fall below print contrast at 1-count level; darken the amber or thicken to 2 px. [major] None of the multi-panel figures carries panel letters (a,b,c...), which Nature requires for caption cross-reference. [minor] "sample" axes never state 200 ps/sample (5 GS/s); "ADC-eq" is used consistently but defined nowhere on-figure. [minor] Font sizes are consistent in family (Helvetica) but not in size across figures — Integrity_health and Integrity_waveforms labels are ~40% smaller than BestTiming at equal print width. Single-column survivability: only MCPThreshold, XCETCheck, ElectronID and BestTiming survive single-column; Integrity_waveforms (18 panels, 5 of them EMPTY) and TransferFit (8 panels) are double-column/supplement scale and should be declared as such. BEST TWO: BestTiming.png (complete labeling, quantitative legend, clear fit annotation, accessible palette) and MCPThreshold.png (clean, self-captioning, threshold line + value annotation, only a nit-level text/line graze). WORST TWO: QCv2_align.png (garbled title, no legend on a five-color ROOT-default panel, missing y label) and QCv2_MIP.png (all four titles reduced to clipped glyph debris, no y labels, black-on-black fit indistinguishable from data, no per-panel channel ID — the four panels cannot be told apart). Both worst figures look like they predate radStyle.h adoption; regenerating them through the house style is the single highest-leverage action for the whole site.

plots.what_it_shows: 3x6 grid of per-channel waveform persistence maps (orange density heat, teal median overlay) for all 18 DRS4 channels: XCET40/43, ScintA, LG 4-7, TR0 g0/g1, HG(4)-(7), and five EMPTY channels. Common y-range (ADC-eq, roughly -2500 to +3300) and x = sample 0-1024.
plots.caption_issues: In-panel titles (channel index + name) are accurate and consistent. However 'sample' is given without the 200 ps/sample conversion, the persistence z-scale (what orange density means, how many events overlaid) is stated nowhere, and 'ADC-eq' is undefined on-figure. Panels 2, 8 and 17 have data clipped below the y-range floor with no 'clipped' note.
plots.design_issues: [major] Five EMPTY panels (3, 9, 10, 11, 12) consume ~28% of the figure area as dead space — drop them or collapse to a one-line 'channels 3, 9-12 empty' note; a journal will not print five blank axes. [major] No colorbar/z-scale for the persistence density; the heat map is uninterpretable quantitatively. [major] At 18 panels the axis numerals are ~5 pt at double-column width — fails print legibility; this figure cannot survive any reduction and should be flagged supplement-only. [minor] Panel-title text ('5 LG 5', '13 HG(5)') sits directly on top of the data cloud in the LG/HG panels — add a white text box or move above the frame. [minor] Bottom clipping in ScintA and both TR0 panels hides the full negative excursion; either extend y or annotate. [nit] Redundant 'ADC-eq' y title repeated 18 times; shared row labels would clean the grid.
plots.physics_questions: Median pulse-peak sample differs strongly by group (XCET/ScintA ~440-500, LG ~390, TR0 ~50, HG ~60) — are these fixed DRS group latency offsets, and are they removed before the srCFD timing? TR0 g0/g1 show a persistent positive rail band (~+400 ADC-eq) after the pulse — undershoot/rail artifact worth a caption note. ScintA is negative-polarity while calorimeter channels are positive — inverted on purpose?

plots.what_it_shows: Four channel-indexed summary bars (x = channel 0-17): baseline RMS (log y), signal fraction with amp>150 cut, rail fraction (log y), and median pulse-peak sample with two red dashed reference lines.
plots.caption_issues: In-panel titles are accurate but incomplete: panel 2's title 'signal fraction (amp > 150)' is partially obscured by the channel-8 bar rising through it; the two red dashed lines in panel 4 (near sample ~30 and ~990, presumably the acceptance window) are explained nowhere; no panel states that x is DRS channel index.
plots.design_issues: [major] No axis titles anywhere: all four y-axes untitled, x-axis untitled ('channel index' missing) — for a bare-numbers grid this is disqualifying in print. [major] Text/data collision: the panel-2 title is overprinted by the ch-8 bar; move titles above the frame or add opaque background. [major] The canvas is ~25% empty margin (large blank band below the panels, wide right gutter) — wasted print area that forces the actual panels smaller; crop the canvas. [minor] Red dashed reference lines (panel 4) have no key. [minor] Mixed log (panels 1, 3) and linear (2, 4) y scales with no visual cue beyond tick labels — add '(log)' to titles. [nit] Pale teal fill at this size is fine, but tick label font is smaller than every other figure in the set.
plots.physics_questions: Rail fraction is nonzero (up to ~7e-3) in EMPTY channels 9-12 — pickup, or an artifact of the rail definition on flat baselines? Signal fraction saturates at 1.0 for ch 8 and 13-17 (TR0 + HG): is that expected for a threshold of 150 on high-gain/noisy channels, i.e., is the cut meaningful there at baseline RMS ~100?

plots.what_it_shows: 2x2 grid of log-y amplitude spectra (amp [ADC-eq], 0-2000), one per capillary channel, each with a black fit curve (Landau-like) over the peak region ending near 1000, with an unfitted flat tail beyond.
plots.caption_issues: All four panel titles are clipped at the canvas top edge and render as illegible glyph fragments — the panels cannot be identified (which capillary is which is unrecoverable from the figure). This is a hard production failure. Additionally, given the campaign finding that MIP normalization is invalid (species + noise-estimator bias, documented in Output/run_12/FINDINGS.md), the figure carries no deprecation/context note.
plots.design_issues: [critical] Clipped/garbled titles on all four panels — likely a ROOT title pave positioned above the frame; move the title inside the frame per house style (cf. TransferFit.png) and regenerate for all 14 runs. [critical] No panel identification (capillary number) survives, so the 2x2 grid is anonymous. [major] No y-axis title on any panel (events? events/bin?). [major] Fit curve is solid black on a solid black histogram — indistinguishable in grayscale and barely in color; use the house teal or red, or dash it, and add a two-entry legend. [major] No fit annotation (MPV, range, chi2) — the panel communicates nothing quantitative. [minor] Fit visibly departs from data above ~600 and stops arbitrarily near 1000 with no fit-range indicator. [nit] x-axis titled on all four panels; once per column would suffice.
plots.physics_questions: Since MIP normalization was proven invalid for cross-run gain tracking, does this figure still belong in the standard 9, or should it be retitled as a QC shape check with an explicit 'not used for normalization' note? What population is the un-fitted flat tail at 1000-2000 ADC-eq (shower fragments under the MIP selection?).

plots.what_it_shows: 2x4 grid, one column per capillary (4-7). Top: HG peak spectrum (log y) with orange dotted digitizer 'wall' marker and red clip-wall edge line. Bottom: HG vs LG scatter (blue density), black profile points, teal linear fit with dashed extrapolation, beige shading of the fit region, per-panel fit equation (e.g. 'HG = 301 + 2.39 LG') and fit-range annotation; legend in the first bottom panel.
plots.caption_issues: In-panel annotations are accurate and unusually complete (fit equation, fit window, wall definition). Minor: the top-row red text 'wall 3143' etc. does not state units, and 'HG < 0.72 wall' requires the reader to do arithmetic; consider printing the resulting cut value.
plots.design_issues: [major] Top row: the red 'wall NNNN' annotation is overprinted on the histogram bars and grazes the orange dotted line in every panel (worst in capillary 7, where it collides with data at the plateau) — move to the top margin with a white box. [major] Orange 'fit: LG 30-815...' text sits on the beige shaded region — orange-on-tan is the lowest-contrast text in the whole set and will die in print; recolor to the dark red or black. [minor] Top-row log-y axis shows only decades 1 and 10 with unlabeled minor ticks up to ~40 — add the top decade label. [minor] Legend appears only in bottom-left panel; acceptable, but then panels need letters (a-h) so a caption can point to it. [minor] 8 panels means double-column only; at single column the blue density squares vanish. [nit] Teal fit line over blue density is distinguishable but close in hue for deuteranopes; the dashed extrapolation is barely visible where it exists.
plots.physics_questions: HG/LG transfer slopes span 2.39-2.83 (~17%) across the four capillaries — is that spread folded into the +-15% cross-run gain-ladder systematic already documented, or is it an independent per-channel term? Why is capillary 7's linear fit window capped at LG 695 while the others reach ~800 — earlier saturation on that channel?

plots.what_it_shows: Two log-y MCP peak-amplitude spectra (TR0 group 0 full range 0-4000; TR0 group 1 zoomed 0-2000), pale teal fill, red vertical turn-on line with annotation 'turn-on: 976 ADC-eq = 238 mV'.
plots.caption_issues: Accurate and self-captioning; the '(zoom)' qualifier on the right panel honestly flags the truncated x-range. Only gap: the right panel's tail is still ~30 events/bin at the 2000 edge, so a reader cannot see where group 1 ends — one clause ('tail extends to ~X') would close it.
plots.design_issues: [minor] Left panel: the red annotation text ends where the red turn-on line rises, and the line passes through the tail of '= 238 mV' — nudge the text left or the line's label up. [minor] Right panel x-range clips a still-populated tail; either match the left panel's range in an inset or annotate the cutoff. [nit] Red line + red text is the only key; a one-line legend entry would be more conventional. [nit] Sub-threshold single events at ~850-950 are visible but unremarked. Otherwise this is the cleanest figure of the nine and survives single-column reduction without change.
plots.physics_questions: The turn-on threshold sits on the rising edge of the amplitude distribution (peak at ~1050, threshold 976) — what fraction of true MCP hits is lost, and is the timing-reference sample biased toward larger amplitudes (better MCP resolution) as a result? A handful of events below turn-on survive — leakage through a different trigger path?

plots.what_it_shows: Two log-y XCET threshold-Cherenkov amplitude spectra (XCET 40 in teal, XCET 43 in orange, both annotated '0.21 bar') with a dark-red dashed vertical line at the current 150 ADC-eq electron-tag cut and a red text key.
plots.caption_issues: Accurate; 'dashed: current 150 ADC-eq cut' is an honest, unambiguous key. The pedestal spike at ~0-20 and the secondary spike near ~55 in XCET 43 go unexplained — worth a caption clause since the cut placement argument depends on the valley being clean.
plots.design_issues: [major] The two panels use different histogram colors (teal vs orange) for no encoded reason — the panel titles already identify the counters, so the color change reads as a series distinction that does not exist; unify or state the mapping. [major] The thin orange outline of XCET 43 at the 1-5 event level is near-invisible on white in print — the amber needs darkening or a 2 px stroke (recurring house-palette problem). [minor] Red text key and dark-red dashed line are close but not identical hues; make them match exactly. [nit] y-axis 'events' has no bin width; 'events / N ADC-eq' preferred. Survives single-column.
plots.physics_questions: XCET 40's valley between pedestal and Cherenkov plateau bottoms out at only ~5-10 events against a plateau of ~20-40 — what mis-tag probability does the 150 cut imply per counter, and is the two-counter coincidence quoted anywhere on-page? What is the sharp secondary spike at ~55 ADC-eq in XCET 43 (afterpulse/ringing)?

plots.what_it_shows: Three normalized comparison panels of XCET-tagged electrons (red, beige fill) vs off-coincidence events (blue): shower sharing (max LG / sum LG), prompt/slow balance (sum HG / sum LG), and total LG energy (sum LG), legend in the first panel.
plots.caption_issues: Accurate. 'prompt / slow balance' as a title for sum HG / sum LG is jargon that the axis label does not resolve — a reader outside the group cannot connect the ratio to prompt vs slow light without the run page text.
plots.design_issues: [major] Third panel: the blue off-coincidence spike terminates exactly at the y-axis maximum (0.30) — it is at best flush with the frame and at worst clipped; extend the y-range or annotate the peak value, since a clipped peak in a normalized comparison misrepresents the contrast. [minor] Legend only in panel 1 without panel letters (a/b/c) for the caption to reference. [minor] The red and blue are acceptable for common CVD types, but the beige fill under red is very close to the TransferFit fit-region beige used with a completely different meaning — cross-figure semantic collision in the same 9-figure set. [nit] fraction/bin y title is good; add bin width for the third panel since bins are visibly nonuniform in impact. Survives single-column.
plots.physics_questions: Tagged electrons sit at lower sum HG / sum LG than off-coincidence events — is that HG clipping at the ~13.6k LG headroom ceiling for big showers, or a genuine species difference exploitable as a second ID variable? The tagged (red) sum LG distribution retains a small population near zero — tag-but-no-shower events (upstream conversion, scatter-out), and are they cut before timing?

plots.what_it_shows: Left: linear-y sum LG spectrum for (apparently) tagged electrons, black outline, title clipped. Right: log-y per-channel pulse-peak-sample (or hit-time) distributions overlaid in five ROOT default colors (red, green, blue, black, two grays) across sample 0-1024, no legend, title clipped.
plots.caption_issues: Both canvas-top titles are cut off by the canvas edge — the left title survives only as a smeared half-height 'electrons sum LG' fragment, the right title is entirely unreadable. Combined with the absent legend on the right panel, the figure cannot be interpreted standalone: five curves with no identification, and the reader cannot even confirm what quantity is plotted.
plots.design_issues: [critical] No legend on a five-series overlay drawn in ROOT default colors — the single worst legibility failure in the set; label every curve (channel/group) or split into small multiples. [critical] Clipped canvas-top titles on both panels (same TPaveText bug as QCv2_MIP); move titles inside the frame. [major] Red+green curve pairing is not colorblind-safe and both grays are nearly identical — switch to the house teal/orange/red/dark palette used everywhere else; this figure and QCv2_MIP are visibly off-style. [major] Left panel has no y-axis title (events?). [minor] 'sample' x-title without the ns conversion. [minor] Left panel linear-y while every comparable spectrum in the set is log-y — inconsistent, hides the tail. [nit] Right panel frame is cramped against the canvas edge, unlike the generous margins elsewhere.
plots.physics_questions: Right panel: the flat red distribution at ~100 events/bin across all 1024 samples looks like a channel whose 'peak sample' is essentially random — noise-dominated channel, or the ambient-light-leak baseline documented in FINDINGS.md? The black (~450) and gray (~510) peak-sample populations are offset by ~60 samples (~12 ns) — inter-group alignment constants, and are they applied upstream of the srCFD timing? Left panel: the spike at sum LG ~150 inside an 'electrons' selection — pedestal leakage through the tag?

plots.what_it_shows: Left: per-capillary srCFD time vs TR0 (delta-t minus median, ns), four overlaid step histograms (teal/blue/amber/red) with a legend quoting per-capillary widths (375/408/312/356 ps). Right: 4-capillary mean shower time with Gaussian fit (red) on a filled histogram, annotated sigma = 248 +/- 8 ps (incl. MCP+DRS).
plots.caption_issues: Accurate, with one ambiguity: the legend values 'cap 4 (375 ps)' never say what the number is (sigma? Gaussian core? RMS?) — the right panel says sigma explicitly, the left should too. The beam energy of run 15 appears nowhere on the figure, which matters since these widths feed the 389/sqrt(E)+138 ps trend.
plots.design_issues: [minor] Left panel: four thin overlaid step histograms with heavy overplotting in the core; the amber (cap 6) line is the low-contrast house amber again and blue vs teal are adjacent hues for CVD readers — thicken lines or offset styles (one dashed). [minor] Legend widths need the sigma symbol and the estimator name. [minor] Add run energy (and run number) to the in-panel annotation so the figure is self-contained across the 14 run pages. [nit] Right panel red fit over black outline + teal fill is the house look and works; consider printing the fit range. This figure and MCPThreshold are the production-quality benchmarks of the set; both survive single-column.
plots.physics_questions: Both panels show a distinct early shoulder at delta-t ~ -1 to -1.5 ns (clearest in the left panel at 10-15 events/bin) that the Gaussian fit excludes — is this the pion/halo contamination population, and is it cut before the quoted sigma = 248 ps or merely ignored by the fit range? Cap 6 is notably narrower (312 ps) than cap 5 (408 ps) — same pattern in other LuAG runs, i.e., a real capillary-to-capillary optical difference rather than statistics?
